channel.title: The Dudley Blog
channel.description: Culture, archetypes, and honest app roundups from Dudley Development — the studio behind Vibe Rater and Monetary Policy: Independence Day.

item.title: Can Your iPhone Prove a Photo Is Real?
item.description: New iPhone provenance ideas could make some photos easier to authenticate, but they are not magic AI detectors. Here is what photo proof means for AI images, social posts, and vibe-check apps.

item.title: Can Apps See Hidden Photos on iPhone?
item.description: Hidden photos are locked in the Photos app, and iPhone photo permissions still matter. Here is what apps can see, what Photo Picker protects, and how to share one image safely.

item.title: What Is Captured by Me on iPhone?
item.description: Captured by Me is a reported iOS 27 Photos collection for pictures taken with your iPhone camera. Here is what it means for finding cleaner photos to edit, share, or use in photo apps.

item.title: Can Smart Glasses Record You?
item.description: Smart glasses can record photos or video from the wearer's point of view, so consent, posting choices, and app privacy settings matter. Here is the practical privacy check before filming or sharing group moments.

item.title: What Is a Vibe Check?
item.description: A vibe check is a quick read on the mood, energy, or social fit of a person, place, photo, or moment. Here is what it means, how to use it, and where playful vibe apps fit.

item.title: What Does Aura Mean in Slang?
item.description: Aura slang means cool presence, social energy, or the imaginary points people gain and lose online. Here is how aura points work and how to use the term without taking it too seriously.

item.title: Do AI Photo Apps Need AI Act Labels?
item.description: The EU AI Act transparency rules start applying on August 2, 2026. Here is what AI photo app users should know about labels, deepfakes, and honest vibe-check posts.

item.title: What Is AI Slop?
item.description: AI slop is low-effort AI-generated content that makes feeds feel fake, repetitive, or misleading. Here is what it means for photo trends, social apps, and vibe-check posts.

item.title: Can AI Use Your Instagram Photos?
item.description: Meta pulled back a July 2026 feature that let people reference public Instagram accounts in AI images, but public social photos still deserve careful privacy settings and context.

item.title: Should You Give an AI Photo App Full Photo Access?
item.description: Most AI photo apps do not need your whole camera roll for a single edit, aura card, or vibe check. Here is when full photo access makes sense and when to use a picker instead.

item.title: Can Photo Apps See Your Location?
item.description: Photo apps may receive location metadata when you share or upload an image. Here is how iPhone photo location data works and what to check before using an aura or AI photo app.

item.title: Do AI Photo Apps Need Labels on TikTok?
item.description: TikTok asks creators to label realistic AI-generated or significantly AI-edited content. Here is what that means before you share AI photo, aura, or vibe-check results.

item.title: Can Apps See All Your iPhone Photos?
item.description: iPhone apps can see your full photo library only when you grant full Photos access. Here is how Limited Access, Photo Picker, and privacy labels work.

item.title: How to Do a Vibe Check in a Group Chat
item.description: A vibe check in a group chat is a quick way to ask what the room feels like, react to a photo, or turn a moment into a low-stakes game. Here is how to do it without making it weird.

item.title: Are Aura Apps Real? Entertainment vs. Actual Analysis
item.description: Aura apps can be fun, but their photo scores, colors, and archetypes should be treated as entertainment. Here is how to tell playful vibe reads from serious claims.

item.title: The Funniest Photo Rating Apps in 2026, Ranked
item.description: A genuinely honest roundup of the best photo rating apps on iPhone in 2026 — what they actually do, who they're for, and which one is most likely to make you laugh at your own photo.

item.title: The Quiet Luxury Era Is Over — Here's What Actually Won
item.description: Quiet luxury peaked with Succession. By 2024, H&M was selling a 'stealth wealth capsule.' The trend cycle moved on. But the aesthetic's successor isn't what you'd expect — and the archetype remains.

item.title: In Defense of the NPC (It's a Compliment Now)
item.description: NPC started as an internet insult. It became a TikTok content genre. Now 'NPC energy' is a genuine compliment — for people who have mastered the art of not performing for anyone. We explain the full arc.

item.title: What Your Phone Case Says About Your Vibe
item.description: The phone case is the one accessory you chose while panicking about dropping your phone. What that split-second decision reveals about your archetype — according to vibe science (not real science).

item.title: Gorpcore Prophet: The Archetype That Won the 2020s Without Trying
item.description: Gorpcore didn't go mainstream. Everyone else went gorpcore. A look at the decade's most unlikely aesthetic winner — and what separates a Gorpcore Prophet from someone who just owns a vest.

item.title: The Best Satirical iOS Games That Actually Respect Your Intelligence
item.description: Most 'funny' games on the App Store are slot machines with a hat. These six satire games on iPhone are genuinely good — including one about the Federal Reserve.

item.title: What Your Federal Reserve Opinion Says About Your Vibe
item.description: Your gut reaction to a Fed rate decision reveals your archetype. We matched every possible take on monetary policy to a Vibe Rater result.
